BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says çᵉgullâh, it means wealth, closely shut up. That is the sense that runs through its 8 occurrences, from 1 Chronicles to Deuteronomy. The word does not change its meaning to suit the passage; the passage leans on the word.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that çᵉgullâh is worth knowing because God gave us the word for wealth, closely shut up. The word is small; the truth it carries is not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
